Operator: Good day, and welcome to the VeriCast Communications Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to VeriCast Communications' Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Moreno, Chief Commercial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Jamie Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I am excited to share our Q2 results, which reflect our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction. We achieved strong performance across several key areas.

First, our service revenues across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments showed robust growth, with wireless up over 4% year-over-year, broadband accelerating even faster, and enterprise leading the way. Second, we continue to see strong adoption of our new products like 5G fixed wireless access and streaming bundles, leading to millions in incremental revenue and substantial subscriber gains. Third, our EBITDA margins expanded meaningfully thanks to operational leverage and cost efficiencies. Fourth, we generated impressive free cash flow, which we're utilizing effectively for deleveraging and returns. Fifth, our debt levels and leverage ratios continued to improve, strengthening our balance sheet. Sixth, our efforts on dividend sustainability and shareholder returns are delivering compelling yields while supporting growth.

Sarah Patel: Thank you, Jamie. Now, let's move on to the financial results. Our revenue for the quarter reached $14.8 billion, an increase of 6.2% compared to the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA was $6.25 billion, resulting in a margin of 42.3%. We are diligently managing our costs and optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures amounted to $4.6 billion, primarily allocated to 5G infrastructure, fiber deployment, and content acquisition.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, thank you for joining our Q2 earnings call for VeriCast Communications. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our free cash flow generation and utilization, which remains a cornerstone of our financial strength in this capital-intensive telecom and media landscape. Free cash flow—or FCF—is calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, and it best reflects our ability to generate sustainable cash after investing in the network and content that drive our competitive moat.

In Q2, we generated $2.6 billion in free cash flow, up 18% year-over-year and marking our strongest quarterly FCF performance since the pandemic recovery. For the first half of the year, cumulative FCF reached $4.9 billion, surpassing our initial guidance midpoint by 8%. This puts us on track for full-year 2024 FCF of $10.5 to $11.5 billion, incorporating synergies from our recent spectrum acquisitions in the AWS-3 and C-band auctions, now fueling 5G Ultra Wideband deployments similar to those accelerated by Verizon and T-Mobile.

Driving this was operating cash flow of $7.2 billion in Q2, a 12% year-over-year increase, propelled by broadband and wireless service revenue growth. Postpaid mobile ARPU climbed 4% to $52.30, benefiting from premium 5G plans and fixed wireless access ramp-up, where we've added 1.2 million subscribers year-to-date—outpacing trajectories like Charter's Spectrum Mobile. On the media side, our streaming platform, VeriStream, grew paid subscribers to 28 million, up 22% year-over-year, with advertising revenue surging 35% to $450 million, thanks to targeted ad-supported video-on-demand tiers competing with Netflix's ad-supported launch and Disney's Hulu bundle.

Offsetting this was CapEx of $4.6 billion in Q2, or 28% of revenue, within our guided range of 26-29%. We trended down from Q1's $4.9 billion as 5G core upgrades moderated following successes in our Open RAN pilots with partners like Nokia and Rakuten Symphony. Fiber-to-the-home expansions—now covering 55% of our North American footprint—accounted for 42% of CapEx at $1.9 billion, delivering 2 Gbps symmetric speeds that are attracting multi-gig upgrades from customers switching from Comcast Xfinity.

Regionally, North America contributed 82% of our half-year FCF at $4.0 billion, with wireless EBITDA margins expanding to 48% on spectrum efficiency gains. In Europe, our Vodafone joint venture stake generated $650 million in distributable FCF, up 15% amid 5G Standalone launches in Germany and Italy, though regulatory pressures on wholesale pricing limited some upside. Latin America, through our Millicom integration, added $250 million—our fastest-growing region at 25% year-over-year—driven by 4G/5G hybrid networks in Colombia and Peru, where we've captured 12% market share from América Móvil.

On utilization, our disciplined approach prioritizes deleveraging, shareholder returns, and growth investments—a strategy that's helped us outperform peers like AT&T on net debt-to-EBITDA, now at 2.4x, down from 2.8x a year ago. We prepaid $1.2 billion in debt during Q2, including $800 million on our 4.75% senior notes due 2028, bringing year-to-date paydowns to $2.5 billion. This reduced our cost of debt by 15 basis points and positions us for investment-grade reaffirmation from Moody's.

For dividends, our quarterly payout of $0.65 per share totaled $1.1 billion, a 5% increase from last year, yielding 4.2%—attractive compared to T-Mobile's lower payout amid their Sprint integration unwind. We deployed $900 million in share repurchases under our $5 billion authorization, retiring 2.1% of shares outstanding at an average price of $42.50, accreting EPS by 3% for the full year on top of organic growth.

The balance, roughly $1.2 billion year-to-date, funded tuck-in acquisitions like the $450 million purchase of EdgeCast CDN assets to strengthen VeriStream's low-latency delivery for live sports streaming—essential as Peacock and Paramount+ compete for NFL and NBA rights. We're also allocating $500 million for network slicing pilots in enterprise 5G private networks, targeting sectors like manufacturing and healthcare with ARPU potential over $100 per month.

Looking ahead, FCF trends are positive. We expect CapEx to peak in the second half at $9.5-10 billion full-year, tapering to $8.5-9 billion in 2025 as 5G coverage reaches 95% and we shift to opex-heavy AI-driven orchestration through our Ericsson partnership. Media tailwinds from bundling VeriStream with wireless services, akin to Discovery's Max integration, should add $300 million in incremental FCF by year-end. While risks like supply chain delays on Open RAN radios or potential FCC mid-band refarming exist, our $3.2 billion liquidity and undrawn revolver offer strong protection.

As we wrap up a transformative period in telecom and media, our commitment to dividend sustainability and shareholder returns stands out. For the trailing 12 months, we declared and paid $2.48 per share in dividends, our 18th consecutive year of increases—a 4% hike from prior year, outpacing inflation and targeting 3-5% compound annual growth through the decade. This yields 4.2% at current prices, competitive with Verizon at 6.5% and Comcast at 3.1%, but with better growth outlook. Total cash dividends reached $5.2 billion, covered 2.1x by our $11.0 billion in full-year free cash flow, up 12% year-over-year from wireless growth and easing capex.

Beyond dividends, we repurchased $2.8 billion in shares last year, retiring 2.1% of outstanding float at $118 average, for combined returns of $8.0 billion—a 73% FCF payout ratio within our 60-80% target. This total shareholder yield of 7.8% exceeds the S&P 500 Communications Services index average of 4.9%.

Sustainability is backed by layers: adjusted EPS of $5.92 covers at 42% payout, versus AT&T's higher ratio post-spin. FCF per share rose 15% to $20.41, with leverage at 2.1x net debt-to-EBITDA, providing $15 billion in dry powder for returns or M&A like our $1.2 billion Southeast fiber acquisition.

Capex of $9.5 billion—or 28% of revenue—peaked 5G Standalone deployment and C-band use, now live across 95% of U.S. footprint; we guide $8.2-8.5 billion next year, down 12%, leveraging Open RAN with Nokia and Ericsson for 15-20% vendor cost cuts. Media bundles stabilized linear TV churn at 1.2% quarterly.

North America, 75% of FCF, saw U.S. broadband adds of 850,000 for 8% growth, outpacing Charter; FTTH passes 40 million homes at 28% take rates, bundling to retain 85% video subs. Europe’s Vodafone JV saved €450 million, lifting mobile ARPU 4%; Asia-Pacific towers generated $600 million.

Through 'Efficient Growth 2025', we tendered $3 billion high-coupon notes, refinancing sub-4%, saving $120 million interest yearly. AI efficiencies cut opex 7%, lift streaming ads 14%. M&A budget of $4-6 billion targets edge data centers for 12-15% IRR.

We reaffirm $2.58 per share for next year (4% up) and $11.5-12.0 billion FCF, enabling $8.5-9.0 billion returns at 75% payout. ROIC to 11.2% supports 5+ years growth.

Before segments, new product launches drove top-line: $478 million incremental revenue, 32% quarter-over-quarter, 8% of total, with 2.8 million net adds—45% above guidance, strongest since 2021. Blended ARPU up 4.2% to $55.05.

Flagship 5G FWA, nationwide since March post-C-band, added 1.2 million subs, 28% new broadband share per Dell'Oro, $212 million revenue at $80/month unlimited 1 Gbps bundled. 15%+ penetration top DMAs, 22% ARPU premium, 52% EBITDA margins, 1.1% churn via AI slicing.

NovaStream+, ad-supported bundle with live sports, linear, FAST, AI recs, added 1.1 million paid, 4.5 million free-tier; $189 million including $45 million AVOD up 55%, stemmed linear losses to 150,000. $14.50 ARPU, 18% upsell.

5G Mobile Unlimited Max with Disney+/Netflix zero-rated added 500,000 postpaid, $77 million, 22% phone adds boost, ARPU $48.20.

U.S. $385 million (81%), 2.1 million subs at 85% mid-band coverage; Europe $65 million, 450,000 via Vodafone UK; APAC $28 million, 250,000 India.

Launches de-risk OTT fragmentation, 15-20% converged CAGR, 14% churn cut, $450 million capex, 3.8x ROI. Q3 sustains, FWA to 3 million, NovaStream Latin America; 5-7% revenue growth.

As of quarter-end, gross debt $52.4 billion ($48.2 long-term, $4.2 short), net $43.9 billion after $8.5 billion cash, $10 billion undrawn facility. Up $1.2 billion from spectrum repurchases in FCC Auction 110 for 5G capacity.

Net debt to TTM EBITDA 3.2x, down 40 bps quarterly, full turn from 4.2x year-start; TTM EBITDA $13.7 billion up 8%, wireless ARPU $55.40 (+2.8%), Media +12% GlobalStream+ 45 million subs.

Deleveraging accelerates: Q3 FCF $3.1 billion up 15%, $2.5 billion paydowns. Refinanced $4 billion 4.25% notes, swapping 5.75% legacy, cost now 4.1%, 85% fixed.

U.S. 2.8x, FWA 1.2 million adds; Europe 3.8x but Vodafone synergies €500 million; APAC 2.5x.

FY24 capex $18-19 billion (14% revs), below 3.0x YE25 via $3 billion tower sales, accretive M&A like $800 million Mexico fiber, edge for 20% uplift.

$15 billion maturities through 2027 refinancable sub-5%. 3.2x supports $5 billion buybacks, 4.8% yield.

Now, EBITDA margins: consolidated 42.3%, up 280 bps year-over-year from 39.5%, 120 bps sequential from 41.1%; TTM 41.7%, ahead 40-42% guide, beating Verizon ~40%, Comcast 42.8%. Sixth straight expansion quarter.

Revenue +6.2%; wireless ARPU +2.8% $52.40, 450,000 FWA adds (+35%), +150 bps; broadband fiber ARPU +4.1% $78.50, 62% gigabit, 1.1 million locations, +7.5% rev, margins 48.2% (+450 bps), CPI down 15%.

Media VeriStream +1.2 million to 28.4 million, $14.20 ARPU bundled 'StreamFi'; $220 million ads +22%.

OPEX savings $450 million YTD (2.1% below), +200 bps: network opex -18% slicing energy -25%; Nokia/Ericsson $120 million; SAC -12% $320; content -8%.

Headwinds: spectrum 50 bps, content +9% 80 bps; Europe tailwind +300 bps.

U.S. 65% expansion, 45%+ urban; Europe 38.5% to 42%; APAC roaming +15%.

From 37.2% 2022, +180 bps annual; $2.5 billion capex efficiency, 28% rev vs 30%, Open RAN 40% sites, zero-touch -30% rolls.

FWA to 5 million 60%+ margins, AI churn sub-1%, $1.2 billion fiber 15% ROIC, content JVs. Risks FCC hikes, ad softness; 2.3x leverage flexible. On track 42-44% full-year, Q3 42.5-43.0%.

Service revenues $14.2 billion, +7.1% year-over-year—11th straight quarter, ahead industry. Wireless 63% mix, +4.2% to $8.9 billion: 512,000 postpaid phones (78.4 million base), ARPU +2.9% $52.47, 62% premium 5G, 285 Mbps speeds +25% T-Mobile; prepaid +1.8%, churn 0.92% AI retention -15%.

Broadband +7.8% $3.1 billion > Comcast 5.2%: 421,000 adds (fiber 218,000 FWA 203,000), 32 million FTTH pass 4.2 million gigabit, ARPA $68.23 +3.4%, 92% video attach; FWA 1.8 million $45 ARPU 22% pen.

Enterprise +12.5% $2.2 billion: 1,200 adds 340 >$1M ACV, private 5G 18% $250 million run-rate, SD-WAN 9%, ARPU $142,000 +6.2%; Europe 15%.

Core +9.3% ex-legacy; raise FY +6.5%. Balanced: wireless stable, broadband scale, enterprise upside.

Mike Chen: Thank you. I would like to provide an update on our network performance and expansion. We continue to enhance our 5G network, achieving wider coverage at 95% in key markets and faster speeds averaging over 280 Mbps. Our network reliability remains high at 99.99%, and we are investing in advanced technologies like Open RAN with Nokia and Ericsson, network slicing for IoT and edge computing, and AI orchestration to cut energy costs by 25% and truck rolls by 30%. Fiber expansions pass 55% of footprint with 2 Gbps symmetric, supporting FWA ramp and enterprise private networks. We're optimizing for emerging apps, partnering on satellite SOS and mmWave densification.

Lisa Moreno: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We saw strong growth in subscriber additions—2.8 million net across postpaid, broadband, streaming—driven by innovative offerings like 5G FWA (1.2 million adds), NovaStream+ bundles (1.1 million paid), and Unlimited Max plans (500,000). Customer satisfaction scores hit record highs, with churn at 1.3% overall, down 14% year-over-year via AI personalization. We're improving experience across touchpoints, expanding partnerships for Disney/Netflix zero-rated data, UFC/Premier League rights, and unified billing boosting cross-sell 25%. Bundled services enhance value, stemming cord-cutting.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. During this time, we invite you to ask questions by pressing star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your subscriber acquisition costs and your strategy for reducing churn, specifically with regards to the new 5G FWA service?

Lisa Moreno: Thanks for the question, John. Our SAC for FWA came in at $320 this quarter, down 12% year-over-year through AI-optimized marketing and bundling with existing wireless. Churn is exceptionally low at 1.1% monthly versus industry 2.5%, thanks to network slicing ensuring low-latency for gaming and work. We're targeting sub-1% long-term with predictive retention offers, and early LTV shows 3.8x ROI payback.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for leveraging AI and automation to improve network efficiency and reduce operational costs, and how does that impact EBITDA margins?

Mike Chen: Great question, Emily. AI is core to our strategy: predictive maintenance cuts opex 7%, zero-touch orchestration reduces truck rolls 30%, and customer care chatbots lower SAC. For networks, generative AI optimizes slicing and energy, down 25% on diesel post-weather events. This drives our 280 bps margin expansion to 42.3%, with more from Open RAN vendor savings 15-20%. Expect continued 100-200 bps annual gains.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Can you discuss the regulatory environment and any potential impacts on your business, including spectrum refarming and EU Digital Markets Act effects?

Jamie Thompson: Thanks, David. Regulatory remains navigable: FCC mid-band refarming risks are buffered by our $3.2 billion liquidity and strong C-band position. In Europe, DMA hurdles are offset by Vodafone JV synergies and 5G SA traction in Spain/Germany. Wholesale relief in UK boosts margins 300 bps. Overall, we're positioned resiliently with diversified revenue, investment-grade trajectory, and focus on compliant 5G leadership.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Jamie, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Jamie Thompson: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities. We are confident in our ability to deliver sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
